h1:
Bangkok to Hua Hin
A Weekend Beach Road Trip
intro: Hua Hin is the beach Bangkokers can drive to without booking time off work. It's about 230 km, an easy 3-hour drive if the roads cooperate. We've put together a weekend plan, Saturday-Sunday (2 days, 1 night), that takes you from an early-morning departure to beachfront seafood, a night market stroll, and a climb up Khao Takiab, then home before it gets too late. It's a real timeline you can follow.

blocks.html: The nice thing about Hua Hin is that it's close enough to Bangkok to do as a day trip if you really wanted to. But if you want the stay to feel worth it, one night over Saturday-Sunday is just right. Drive down early on day one, soak up the beach and seafood, then hit the market in the evening. On day two, wake up to the sea breeze, grab your photo spots, and start driving back in the afternoon to beat the return traffic.

blocks.text: Before You Go: Routes and Timing Worth Knowing

blocks.html: The main route is Rama 2 → Phetkasem (Highway 35 onto Highway 4), passing Samut Sakhon, Phetchaburi, and Cha-am before reaching Hua Hin. It's normally a 3-hour drive, but right now Rama 2 still has elevated-expressway construction in stretches, and traffic builds up easily, especially Saturday mornings and Sunday evenings. On long-weekend holidays, give yourself an extra 1-1.5 hours to be safe.

items: Leave before 7 a.m. — Rama 2 is still clear at that hour, and you'll reach Hua Hin before noon, in time for a beachfront lunch.

You can bypass Rama 2 — if traffic is really bad, you can cut through Bang Khae, Ekkachai, and Setthakit 1 Road to come out at Samut Sakhon, though there are more traffic lights. Only worth it when Rama 2 is genuinely jammed.
Fill up the tank before Phetchaburi — there are stations along Phetkasem, but queues get long on holidays, so it's easier to fill up while you're still in town.
Have Easy Pass / M-Flow ready — if you use the expressway at the start in Bangkok, it's smoother than paying cash.

blocks.title: The honest truth, between friends
blocks.html: The 3-hour drive assumes clear roads. On long holidays (New Year, Songkran, consecutive holidays), Rama 2 has taken 5-6 hours. If your trip lands on a real long weekend, leave by 5 a.m. or take the train/van instead for peace of mind.

blocks.text: Day 1 (Saturday): Beach, Seafood, and the Night Market

blocks.label: Day 1 · Saturday
blocks.title: Drive down to Hua Hin + seafood + Cicada Market

items.note: Head out early to dodge Rama 2 traffic. You can grab coffee and breakfast at a station around Samut Sakhon.

items.activity: Stop at Cha-am / Cha-am Beach for a quick dip
items.note: It's about 25 km before Hua Hin. If you'd rather not stop, just drive straight on into Hua Hin.
Most places check in at 2 p.m., but you can usually drop bags earlier. Just ask reception.
See our recommended spots in the next section. Steamed blue crab, grilled prawns, and deep-fried sea bass with fish sauce are popular orders.

items.activity: Swim at Hua Hin Beach / relax by the sea
items.note: Check the warning flags before going in. The waves and wind can pick up at times, especially during monsoon season (May-Oct).

items.activity: Back to the hotel, shower, change
items.note: A short nap to save energy for the evening market.
Open Friday-Saturday-Sunday only, roughly 16:00-23:00, near Khao Takiab in front of the Hyatt entrance. Craft stalls, food, and a live music stage.

items.activity: Head back / carry on to Hua Hin Night Market if you're still up for it
items.note: The night market in town is open daily. Good for a snack to round off the evening.

blocks.text: Hua Hin Seafood: Where People Actually Eat

blocks.html: Hua Hin is a seafood town, with everything from scenic beachfront restaurants to humble, budget-friendly spots. We picked these from reviews by people who've actually eaten there, and from places that are still open. Prices are rough ranges and depend on weight and the season of the catch.

items.name: Aroy @ Hua Hin
items.blurb: A big restaurant in the center of town with a long menu of seafood and Thai dishes, quick service, and plenty of room for a group. Popular orders are tom yum goong and steamed blue crab.
items.meta: In Hua Hin town · easy parking

items.name: Krua Nong New
items.blurb: A well-known seafood spot near the road up to Khao Takiab. Homey atmosphere, fresh ingredients, with live crab and prawns to choose from, and friendly prices.
items.meta: On the way up to Khao Takiab

items.name: Mong Doo Lay 77
items.blurb: A beachfront seafood restaurant with open views. The standouts are deep-fried sea bass with fish sauce, fried prawns with tamarind sauce, and steamed blue crab.

items.name: Laciana by the Sea
items.blurb: An Italian-seafood spot right by the sea with a relaxed feel, good for couples or a special meal. It does seafood, Isaan food, and has a cafe all in one place.

items.name: Seafood stalls around Chatchai Market / Night Market
items.blurb: If you want cheap, street-style eats, the night market in the center of town has plenty of grilled and steamed seafood stalls you can order from on the spot.

blocks.title: Ordering seafood without overpaying
blocks.html: Blue crab and prawns are priced by weight. Before you order, ask the price per kilo and have them weigh it in front of you so the bill doesn't catch you off guard. Beachfront restaurants with nice views tend to cost a bit more than the ones tucked down a soi, the trade-off for the setting.

blocks.text: Day 2 (Sunday): Khao Takiab, Photo Spots, Then Drive Home

blocks.label: Day 2 · Sunday
blocks.title: Khao Takiab + the train station + drive back

items.activity: Wake to the sea breeze, walk the beach by your hotel
items.note: The sea is usually calmer in the morning than in the afternoon, good for photos and a stroll.

items.activity: Breakfast at the hotel / a beachfront cafe
items.note: Hua Hin has plenty of beachfront cafes. Sip a coffee in the breeze before you start the day.

items.activity: Climb Khao Takiab, pay respects at the temple, take in the bay view
items.note: There are tons of monkeys here. Watch out for them snatching things. Don't carry plastic bags or visible food, and keep your glasses and phone tucked away.

items.activity: Stop by Hua Hin Railway Station for photos
items.note: The historic wooden station, recently restored, with the Royal Waiting Room of King Rama VI, is the town's classic photo spot.
Hua Hin souvenirs include shrimp paste, fish sauce, salted fish, and Phetchaburi custard cake (mor kaeng) you can pick up on the way home.

items.activity: Hit the road back to Bangkok
items.note: Leaving in the afternoon dodges the Sunday-evening return wave. If you leave after 4 p.m., Rama 2 starts to get packed.
Add an hour or so if it's a long weekend.

blocks.text: Which Area Should You Stay In?

blocks.html: Hua Hin has several areas to stay, so pick based on your trip style. Room rates swing with the season and holidays: weekdays are cheaper than weekends, and long weekends are the priciest. Booking ahead usually gets you a better rate.

items.name: Central Hua Hin
items.blurb: Walking distance to the night market, walking street, and Hua Hin Beach, with little driving needed. Good for those who want convenience.

items.name: Khao Takiab area
items.blurb: Quieter, close to Cicada Market and the seafood restaurants, with a long beach for swimming. Good for a proper rest.

items.name: Cha-am - Pranburi area
items.blurb: Just before or after Hua Hin, with plenty of beachfront resorts. Good for getting away from the bustle, though you'll need to drive into town.

items: Check the car — tire pressure, fuel, and coolant before a long drive.
Book your stay ahead — weekends and long holidays fill up fast and prices jump.
Sunscreen, hat, sunglasses — the Hua Hin sun is strong, especially midday to afternoon.
Cash on hand — some street stalls and market vendors still take only cash / PromptPay.
Pad your timing — Rama 2 is unpredictable. Leaving early and driving back in the afternoon helps a lot.

faq.q: How long does it take to drive from Bangkok to Hua Hin?
faq.a: It's about 230 km, normally around 3 hours if the roads are clear. But Rama 2 still has construction in stretches, so holidays can take 4-5 hours. We'd suggest leaving before 7 a.m. to avoid the traffic.

faq.q: Is a 2-day, 1-night weekend enough time in Hua Hin?
faq.a: Plenty. On day one you cover the beach, seafood, and a night market like Cicada. On day two you climb Khao Takiab, stop at the railway station for photos, grab souvenirs, and drive back in the afternoon. It's a pace that doesn't leave you worn out.

faq.q: What days is Cicada Market open?
faq.a: Cicada Market is open Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays only, roughly 16:00-23:00, near Khao Takiab. If your trip lands on a Saturday or Sunday, the timing works out. If you come on a weekday, this market is closed.

faq.q: Can you swim at Hua Hin Beach, and is it safe?
faq.a: You can swim, but the waves and wind get strong at times, especially during monsoon season (around May-Oct), so check the beach warning flags before going in. The sea is usually calmer in the morning than the afternoon. Young children should have an adult close by.

faq.q: What should you watch out for at Khao Takiab?
faq.a: Khao Takiab has a lot of monkeys that like to grab food and small items. Don't carry plastic bags or visible food, and keep your glasses, phone, and valuables tucked away. If a monkey gets close, don't stare it down, just slowly back away.
